tasks.short: Estimate bicycle repair costs and write the service ticket

steps.what: Assess the requested repair and determine the actual work, parts and labour assumptions
outputs: Repairer's work scope and explicit parts and labour assumptions

steps.what: Capture customer and bicycle details and check actual parts prices and applicable shop labour rates
inputs: Shop-maintained parts and labour price records in bicycle workshop software, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked ticket fields and explicit pricing inputs

steps.what: Stage the ticket's confirmed fields and calculate exact parts and labour subtotals and the estimated total
inputs: Checked fields and pricing inputs from s2
outputs: Staged service ticket and traceable estimated totals

steps.what: Write the actual repair scope, qualifications and estimate wording and check the complete final service ticket
outputs: Complete checked service ticket with estimate clearly distinguished from authorized work

steps.what: Save the checked service ticket
outputs: Saved repair estimate and service ticket

tasks.design: Configure native {OPS_SYSTEM} ticket fields and calculations for the repairer's checked inputs. The repairer writes the actual repair scope and qualifications and checks the entire ticket before saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual ticket assembly and repeated price arithmetic can duplicate known information.
tasks.enabler_now: Native workshop forms and explicit calculation rules can stage confirmed fields and totals.
tasks.still_hard: Repair diagnosis and realistic labour allowances depend on the actual bicycle.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise uncertain work and explain the limits of the estimate.

ambition.what: Improve the existing estimate and service ticket.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: workshop ticket forms can reuse confirmed fields and calculate explicit parts and labour totals; repair assessment remains human.

assumptions: Conditional manual-ticket episode, not a measured baseline. Shop owners maintain price and rate records; customer detail capture and repairer price verification are counted in s2.
Use native features first. Existing automatic totals and fields are baseline; s3 saving applies only where equivalent manual assembly remains.
s4's limited field-reuse reduction leaves substantive scope writing and the complete final check intact. No generated diagnosis, inferred labour time or hidden customer approval.

This task writes the ticket; actual customer estimate transmission, acceptance and repair authorization must be separate checked actions if present in the observed workflow. They are not silently performed or removed here.
Same-system save is negligible and fully retained. Gross 25 plus 6.8 equals 31.8; upkeep 3 gives net 28.8 across 100 illustrative focal effort points.
unknowns: Actual workshop ticket automation and price data quality
research_questions: Which ticket fields and calculations are still performed manually today?

already_counted.description: Repair assessment, actual input capture and retained ticket writing and final checking

incremental.description: Maintain ticket fields and price-calculation mappings

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete ticket checked in s4; any edit requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional manual field and arithmetic saving 31.8 less upkeep 3; zero if native automation already supplies the same result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Identify the exact needed parts and capture quantities and compatibility requirements from actual repair or stock needs
inputs: Actual bicycle repair or stock requirement
Existing workshop and parts records, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Repairer-authored part identifiers, quantities and compatibility requirements

steps.what: Find and check supplier availability, actual prices and delivery terms for the exact required parts
outputs: Checked supplier options with unresolved substitutions marked

steps.what: Stage exact confirmed part identifiers and quantities into the native draft order
inputs: Exact checked supplier matches from s2
outputs: Draft order with traceable item and quantity matches

steps.what: Select the supplier and resolve exceptions, then complete and check the exact order, delivery details and matching order record
inputs: Actual compatibility, price and delivery evidence
outputs: Complete checked order and matching internal record

steps.what: Submit the exact checked parts order to the supplier
outputs: Submitted parts order and actual acknowledgement status

steps.what: Save the checked internal order record with the actual submission status
outputs: Saved parts order record

tasks.design: Use native {PARTNER_PORTAL} search and a staged exact-field order import from {OPS_SYSTEM}. The repairer determines compatibility, chooses the supplier and checks the complete order before the separate supplier submission and internal save.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue navigation and transferring exact part lines can duplicate the repairer's work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native catalogue filters and structured draft-order imports can preserve exact identifiers and quantities.
tasks.still_hard: Part variants, substitutions and delivery tradeoffs require human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Verify compatibility and decide which supplier commitment is appropriate.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: supplier catalogue search and structured draft-order imports can reduce exact-line transfer while retaining human supplier and compatibility decisions.

assumptions: Conditional manual-transfer episode; no measured baseline. Repairer requirement capture is fully counted in s1 and supplier evidence checking in s2; no free normalized order input.
Native features first. Unmatched identifiers, changed terms and substitutions remain in s4; no automatic equivalent-part selection. Existing native ordering automation earns no new saving.
Assumes actual delegated purchasing authority for these parts. Any required owner approval must inspect the complete final order before s5, with their labour added.

Separate save is negligible and fully retained; no new saving for submission, acknowledgement runtime, receipt or payment. If the portal already creates the internal record there is no separate baseline transfer to remove.
All 100 illustrative focal points: gross 4 plus 20 equals 24; upkeep 3 gives net 21. Deduplicate part identification already performed in service-ticket work.
unknowns: Native import availability and actual purchasing authority
research_questions: Is exact-line transfer still manual between the workshop requirement and supplier draft order?

already_counted.description: Requirement capture, supplier evidence checking and complete final-order judgement

incremental.description: Maintain exact identifier mappings and test draft-order staging

approvals.approved_version: Exact complete supplier order checked in s4; any item, price or term change requires recheck
Exact matching internal record checked in s4 plus actual submission status only

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional exact-line transfer and lookup saving 24 less upkeep 3; native-equivalent cases earn zero.

tasks.short: Sell bicycles and accessories through the existing checkout

steps.what: Sell bicycles and accessories by discussing customer needs, explaining options and agreeing the actual selected items
outputs: Customer-selected items and understood terms

steps.what: Find and verify current item prices and availability in the existing shop system
inputs: Shop-maintained inventory and price records in the retail checkout system, defined as OPS_SYSTEM
outputs: Checked price and availability information

steps.what: Enter the actual basket and complete and check its native total, customer-agreed payment, sale record and receipt details
inputs: Actual agreed items and checked prices
Customer's actual purchase and payment choice
outputs: Final checked basket, authorized payment amount, matching sale record and receipt preview

steps.what: Collect the exact checked customer-authorized payment through the existing checkout
inputs: Exact checked amount and customer payment authorization from s3
outputs: Actual payment outcome

steps.what: Commit the checked sale record with the actual payment outcome
outputs: Recorded sale or correctly pending transaction

steps.what: Issue the checked receipt for the actual completed transaction
inputs: Exact receipt details checked in s3
outputs: Customer receipt

tasks.design: Configure native item lookup in {OPS_SYSTEM} while retaining customer discussion and the existing checkout. The repairer checks the exact basket, payment and receipt before the separate payment, sale commit and receipt actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation can slow finding an item's current price and stock.
tasks.enabler_now: Native exact-item filters can reduce that navigation.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding needs and confirming the agreed sale remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Explain options and ensure the customer understands the purchase.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: retail systems provide exact-item lookup and existing checkout totals; improving navigation can support sales conversations.

assumptions: Representative retail-sale episode with an existing checkout, not a measured duty mix. Shop owners maintain source records; actual lookup and verification remain in s2.
Native filters first; existing price totals, payment processing, stock updates and receipt generation are baseline and earn no saving. No additional customer-data feed or new payment integration.

The three transaction consequences are shown separately even if one native checkout action triggers them together; their bookkeeping allocations do not represent new baseline saving. Same-system commit is negligible and fully retained.
Final details exist before s3's check. Changed basket, amount or receipt content requires rechecking before any affected action. A failed payment never becomes a completed-sale receipt.
Deduplicate actual fitting advice shared with 20916; no double saving. All 100 illustrative focal points: lookup saving 4 less upkeep 1 gives net 3.
unknowns: Existing item lookup and checkout flow
research_questions: Does observed native item navigation leave material avoidable lookup effort?

already_counted.description: Retained price lookup and complete transaction checking

approvals.approved_version: Exact customer-authorized payment amount and basket checked in s3
Exact sale checked in s3 with actual payment outcome only; other changes require recheck
Exact receipt checked in s3 for the actual completed transaction; changed content requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional lookup saving 4 less upkeep 1; no new saving for existing checkout automation or transaction commits.

tasks.short: Help customers choose bicycles that fit their size and use

steps.what: Find and verify existing bicycle size and intended-use information for the models being considered
inputs: Manufacturer-produced model information in the existing bicycle catalogue, defined as OTHER
outputs: Relevant checked model information

steps.what: Assess the customer's actual body size, fit and comfort with the bicycles being considered
outputs: Repairer's observations and customer's actual fit feedback

steps.what: Discuss intended bicycle uses, explain fit and model tradeoffs and help the customer choose
inputs: Actual fit feedback and model information
outputs: Customer understanding and selection or decision to consider further

tasks.design: Use native filters in the existing {OTHER} bicycle catalogue to locate manufacturer information. Physical fit assessment and the customer's intended-use discussion remain human.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding model-specific sizing information can involve repeated navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Exact model filters can expose existing source information.
tasks.still_hard: Comfort, fit and intended use require the customer's actual feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Notice fit problems and explain practical tradeoffs in person.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: catalogue filtering can reduce model-information lookup but cannot establish a customer's physical fit or comfort.

assumptions: Conditional episode with manual catalogue navigation; no measured baseline or automatic fit recommendation. Manufacturers produce source specifications; repairer retrieval and source checking are counted in s1.
Native features first; existing filters earn no new saving. No body-image analysis, new sizing feed or generated adjustment procedure.
No separate written fit record, customer message or sale commit is established by this advisory task. Actual sale actions are in 20917; shared advice and lookup are counted once.
All 100 illustrative focal effort points: gross lookup saving 2 less upkeep 0.5 gives net 1.5.
unknowns: Existing model catalogue and actual lookup effort
research_questions: Which model information is repeatedly difficult to find during fitting discussions?

already_counted.description: Retained source lookup and information verification

incremental.description: Maintain model filters and source links

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Conditional lookup saving 2 minus upkeep 0.5; actual fitting and customer advice remain fully retained.
